providers.label: OpenAI

setup.title: How to get an OpenAI API key

steps.text: Open the OpenAI API Keys page and sign in.

link.text: Open the OpenAI API Keys page

steps: Create a new secret key for your project.
Copy the key immediately and paste it into Prompt Builder.
Click “Test connection & load models” to verify it.

providers.help: OpenAI API. Enter your API key, then load the available Vision-capable models.
providers.details: The app validates the key through the provider model endpoint and filters for Vision-capable models.

providers.label: Google Gemini

setup.title: How to get a Google Gemini API key

steps.text: Open Google AI Studio and sign in with your Google account.

steps: Create a new API key (Google AI Studio can create a project for you).
Copy the key, paste it into Prompt Builder, then test the connection.

providers.help: Google Gemini API. Enter your API key, then load the available image-input models.
providers.details: The app loads models from the Gemini API and keeps models that support generateContent with image input.

providers.label: Mistral AI

setup.title: How to get a Mistral API key

steps.text: Open Mistral Studio API Keys and sign in.

steps: Click Create new key and give it a recognizable name.
Copy the key immediately and paste it into Prompt Builder.
Click “Test connection & load models” to verify it.

providers.help: Mistral API with native Vision capability metadata.
providers.details: Prompt Builder reads capabilities.vision from the Mistral model catalog, so only models explicitly marked Vision-capable are shown.

providers.label: Groq

setup.title: How to get a Groq API key

steps.text: Open the Groq API Keys page and sign in.

link.text: Open the Groq API Keys page

steps: Copy the key and paste it into Prompt Builder.
Click “Test connection & load models” to verify it.

providers.help: GroqCloud API. Only Groq models documented for image input are offered.
providers.details: Groq uses an OpenAI-compatible API. The Vision allow-list is configurable because its /models response does not expose a universal Vision capability flag.

providers.label: Ollama
providers.help: Local Ollama server. No API key is required for the standard local endpoint.
providers.details: The app loads installed models and enables only models with Vision capability.

providers.label: OpenRouter

setup.title: How to get an OpenRouter API key

steps.text: Open OpenRouter Keys and sign in.

steps: Copy the key and paste it into Prompt Builder.
Click “Test connection & load models” to verify it.

providers.help: OpenRouter provides one API for many model vendors.
providers.details: Prompt Builder checks model input modalities and shows only models whose metadata explicitly includes image input.

providers.label: OpenAI-compatible

setup.title: How to get an API key
steps: Open your provider’s dashboard or admin panel.
Find API Keys, Access Tokens, or Developer Settings.
Create a key that can access the provider’s model API.
Paste the key here and test the connection.

providers.help: Any provider exposing an OpenAI-compatible /models and /chat/completions API.
providers.details: Use this for compatible gateways or self-hosted inference endpoints.

notes.mock_mode: Mock mode changes analysis/generation behavior only. It does not disable provider connection or Vision model loading.
notes.vision_filtering: Only providers with reliable capability metadata use metadata filtering. Other providers use configurable model-name patterns and exclusions from this file.
notes.credential_storage: Provider API keys are stored per provider in the browser localStorage. GitHub Pages has no server-side secret storage in this mode; keys never go into repository files.
